intro: This course covered the principles of adult Basic Life Support — DRABC, CPR, using an AED, the recovery position and choking.
points: This is awareness only — you cannot become competent by reading, so you must complete hands-on manikin training and yearly refreshers before doing CPR for real.
If someone is unresponsive and not breathing normally, treat it as cardiac arrest, call 999 on speaker and ask for a defibrillator.
Agonal gasps are a sign of cardiac arrest, not recovery — do not let them fool you into waiting; if in doubt, start CPR.
Give high-quality compressions in the centre of the chest, 5 to 6 cm deep at 100 to 120 a minute, letting the chest recoil fully.
Turn the AED on as soon as it arrives, follow its voice prompts, and make sure nobody touches the person during analysis or shock.
If an unresponsive person is breathing normally, place them in the recovery position; for choking, give five back blows then five abdominal thrusts.
